title: Should we remove reversed range for input elements from the spec?
body:
The spec describes that input elements can have a "reversed range" when they have a range with a periodic domain (fixed min and max possible values) and a max attribute which is smaller than the min attribute: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/C/#has-a-reversed-range
The only input element with a periodic domain is `<input type=time>`.

When an input has a reversed range, this clause for validation is used:
> Constraint validation: When an element has a reversed range, and the result of applying the algorithm to convert a string to a number to the string given by the element's value is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the maximum and less than the minimum, the element is simultaneously suffering from an underflow and suffering from an overflow.

This means that any value outside the range in between the max and min is valid. Here is an example: creating a time input which only accepts times outside business hours: `<input type=time max="9:00" min="17:00">`. Any value outside of the range made by the two values, such as 8:00 or 20:00, is valid according to the spec. However, as far as I can tell none of the browsers have ever implemented this.

Recently there was a WPT added for this: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/21103
and bugs filed against chromium and firefox: https://crbug.com/1040344 https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1608010

I filed an intent to ship for chromium to implement the spec here: https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/GTPDv_MQbR0
However, it sounded like there was more interest in removing this functionality from the spec than implementing it because it was never implemented anywhere and there does not seem to be significant interest from web developers. Should we remove it from the spec?

cc @TimothyGu @tkent-google @mfreed7
